sources.entry: BlockWatch by mennanov - A language-agnostic linter (Rust) that keeps co-dependent code, docs, and config in sync, with a Claude Code plugin skill.

summary.one_liner: blockwatch is a language-agnostic Rust linter that lets you declare rules in code comments so that co-dependent code, docs, and config stay in sync, failing pre-commit or CI when they drift.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you wrap lines in start and end tags inside comments and attach rules such as affects, same-as, keep-sorted, keep-unique, line-pattern, line-count, check-ai, and check-lua. The same-as validator compares block contents across files, including whole files, JSON/TOML/YAML keys, Markdown sections, and some language constants, without needing a diff. The affects validator reads a unified diff from stdin and fails when a changed block's target was not also edited. Blocks can also be declared in blockwatch.toml for files that cannot hold comments, such as package.json. The README says it supports 37 languages and their common file names, and it provides a `blockwatch skill` command that prints an agent skill file. Subcommands include list, explain, and --suppress for known violations.
use_cases: keep docs in sync with code
check duplicated values across config files
fail pre-commit when linked code changes
enforce sorted lists in source files
validate code comments and blocks in CI
give AI coding agents project sync rules
how_to_run: pipx install blockwatch-cli # or: uv tool install blockwatch-cli
notable: Rules written as comments next to the code they describe, with no separate config for most blocks
Language-agnostic: covers 37 languages and common file names such as Gemfile, Dockerfile, and Tiltfile
Cross-file same-as and affects validators, including pointers to JSON keys and Markdown sections
Ships an agent skill via `blockwatch skill` and a Claude Code plugin install
Known violations can be suppressed by address with --suppress without editing source
caveats: Deleting a block or its file silently removes its rule; the run does not warn
Files with blocks must be UTF-8; UTF-16 files with tags are skipped silently
Files with unsupported extensions are skipped silently unless mapped with -E or extensions config
keywords: keep code and docs in sync
